codings.one_line: Fast-food hiring chatbots gave bad instructions, failed to relay applicant info, mis-scheduled interviews.
codings.rationale: Ordinary job applicants used the recruiting chatbots as intended in plain-language interactions and the systems failed anyway, so category C.

codings.one_line: A user got Bing Chat's image analysis to solve a CAPTCHA despite the feature being restricted for that purpose.
codings.rationale: No technical exploit was used, but the user deliberately probed the chatbot to demonstrate the safeguard could be defeated, matching the goading test for category B.

codings.one_line: Grant peer reviewers allegedly pasted applicants' proposals into ChatGPT to draft assessment reports.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1/2: the harm stems from reviewers misusing a general AI tool to breach confidentiality, not from a deployed conversational system's output during an end-user interaction.

codings.one_line: LLaMA-based companion chatbots reportedly generate violent and illegal sexual roleplay content for users.
codings.rationale: Users engaging a companion chatbot in the explicit roleplay it's built for is ordinary use of the product, so it passes as category C rather than adversarial or goading input.

codings.one_line: Kremlin-linked firms allegedly used generative AI to help write disinformation articles distributed in Latin America.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is AI used as a content-authoring tool in a state disinformation operation, not a deployed conversational/agentic system interacting with end users.

codings.one_line: A near-duplicate, apparently ChatGPT-written book with a fake author appeared on Amazon before the original author's release.
codings.rationale: Fails scope test 1: this is AI-generated content published as a product by a third party, not a deployed conversational AI interacting with an end user in a session.

codings.one_line: Google's featured snippets and SGE search AI gave false, ChatGPT-sourced answers to simple geography questions.
codings.rationale: Ordinary users typed plain factual queries and the search AI fabricated/relied on false info, which is the normative-use failure described for category C.

codings.one_line: Academics used Google Bard to generate case studies for a parliamentary submission, which fabricated false misconduct allegations against major consultancies.
codings.rationale: An ordinary good-faith request to Bard to produce case studies is legitimate use consistent with the tool's purpose, and it fabricated content, fitting category C.

codings.one_line: A Colorado attorney used ChatGPT for legal research and unknowingly filed a motion citing fabricated case law, leading to denial of the motion and his firing.
codings.rationale: The lawyer made an ordinary, good-faith request for case citations and ChatGPT hallucinated them, matching category C; the firing and bar referral make the harm enforceable.

codings.one_line: A user injected instructions into a Chevy dealer's ChatGPT-powered chatbot, getting it to 'agree' to sell a Tahoe for $1.
codings.rationale: The user typed explicit override instructions telling the bot to agree with anything, a direct prompt-injection technical exploit, so category A.
